title: Ruby on Rails Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: "Hello, Asha!"
end
end
exercises.question: A route names a controller and action. GET /hello runs LessonController#hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The route points to lesson#hello. Rails calls that action and renders plain text. The file lesson_controller.rb must define LessonController.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/book", to: "lesson#book"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def book
 render json: { title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24 }
end
end
exercises.question: render json turns a Ruby value into a JSON response. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The action passes a Ruby hash to render json, which serialises its named fields. Do not call render twice in one action.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello/:name", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: "Hi, #{params[:name]}!"
end
end
exercises.question: A colon marks a route value. GET /hello/Ravi places Ravi in params[:name]. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The route segment is stored in params[:name]. String interpolation reads Ravi from it. Use plain text or safe templates when returning user text.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/search", to: "lesson#search"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def search
 render json: { term: params[:q] || "" }
end
end
exercises.question: params also contains query values. Open GET /search?q=cat. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The query value q is present, so the fallback is not needed. Client parameters need checks before important use.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
post "/books", to: "lesson#create"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def create
 if !params[:title].is_a?(String)
  render json: { error: "Title needed" }, status: :bad_request
  return
 end
 render json: { title: params[:title] }, status: :created
end
end
exercises.question: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. Rails puts body values in params. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The title parameter is a String. The action sends it with created status instead of taking the error branch. This example returns data but does not save a database record.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
post "/books", to: "lesson#create"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def create
 allowed = params.permit(:title)
 render json: allowed
end
end
exercises.question: permit chooses allowed parameter keys. Send POST /books with title and an extra secret key; only title is returned. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: permit selects title and leaves out the unlisted key. Rendering the allowed parameters sends only that field. Permitting a key does not validate its meaning or value.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/missing", to: "lesson#missing"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def missing
 render json: { error: "Book not found" }, status: :not_found
end
end
exercises.question: Rails status symbols name HTTP statuses. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The :not_found symbol chooses HTTP 404 along with the error hash. An error body should come with an error status.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello/:name", to: "lesson#hello", as: :hello
get "/link", to: "lesson#link"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: params[:name]
end
def link
 render plain: hello_path(name: "Asha")
end
end
exercises.question: The as option names a route helper. Open GET /link to see the helper fill in a name. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The named route creates hello_path. Supplying Asha fills its required name segment. Path helper inputs must match the route values.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/start", to: "lesson#start"
get "/hello", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def start
 redirect_to "/hello"
end
def hello
 render plain: "Welcome"
end
end
exercises.question: redirect_to sends a Location header. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: redirect_to sends /hello as the next URL. The client then receives Welcome. Return after a redirect if more code should not run.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/note", to: "lesson#note"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def note
 response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
 render plain: "Practice note"
end
end
exercises.question: response.headers holds reply headers. Open GET /note. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The response header is assigned before render sends the plain text. Set headers before the response is completed.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/school", to: "lesson#school"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
before_action :set_school
def school
 render plain: @school
end
private
def set_school
 @school = "Oak School"
end
end
exercises.question: before_action runs before controller actions. GET /school reads the value set by the callback. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The callback runs first and sets @school for this controller request. The action reads that value. Callbacks can affect many actions, so keep their purpose clear.

exercises.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
delete "/books/:id", to: "lesson#destroy"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def destroy
 head :no_content
end
end
exercises.question: head sends a status and no body. DELETE /books/1 returns 204 in this practice-only action. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: head :no_content selects status 204 and has no JSON or text body. This sample has no stored records; it demonstrates the response shape only.
